scope: C6 unchanged desktop manual input diagnostic, not C7 acceptance, not a display-FPS benchmark. 15 observation windows include four timeline-button interference counterexamples, not 15 equivalent successful crossings.
methodology: Trusted Playwright mouse pointer gestures during measured manual windows; no product API/prototype/source/clock overrides. V2 preparatory placement uses a normal synthetic DOM input event outside the measured span to avoid the already reproduced button overlap.

No screenshots during measured spans. Public renderCount/rafTicks diagnostics update about every 100 ms: deltas indicate submitted renderer work, not GPU completion or physical display frames. Page rAF is separately observed.
Cold means a fresh page/WebGL context; OS, browser disk and GPU driver caches were not forcibly cleared. Warm means revisiting in the same context; repeated texture requests remained observable.

One 1920x1080 context additionally used 1 ms CDP CPU sampling and a trace. Sampling and tracing add overhead. Its timings locate functions and main-thread image decoding; do not treat them as uninstrumented screen FPS.
1920x1080 DPR1 and 2042x1083 DPR1.25 are desktop CSS viewport cases. The latter approximates a 2552x1354 physical screenshot but its original browser CSS size is unknown.

findings.fact: Both desktop viewports reproduced pointerdown on BUTTON at about .78, no input event, and release at the exact node progress .7859741978167384. The range and marker buttons occupy the same vertical band, with marker z-index higher.
findings.consequence: The gesture becomes a discrete node click instead of continuous drag. Keep separate keyboard/click access while separating marker and continuous-track hit areas.

findings.fact: Real canvas forward/reverse and successful timeline gestures showed 100-176ms main-thread stalls. texSubImage2D and nested WebP image decoding dominate the sampled worst tasks, including progress .786 and .871 outside the .844-.855 nonzero Glare interval.
findings.consequence: Investigate explicit asynchronous image decode and bounded pre-upload before first use, retaining original texture bytes, colorspace, flipY, mipmaps and source timing. These are untested candidates, not yet guaranteed improvements.

findings.fact: The actual warm reverse span still requested 14 resources including 10 Glare resources. Its worst task decoded seven WebPs. Active texture memory already exceeded the global 160MiB eviction threshold, so any no-longer-visible/non-prefetched entry is immediately eligible for disposal.
findings.consequence: Evaluate a bounded recent-use allowance separate from unavoidable currently visible bytes, and direction-aware native Glare prefetch. Do not assume a larger unbounded cache is safe.

runs.scope: Actual C6 natural pointer timeline and canvas gestures around c1 .78-.90, versus native rate-1 autoplay; no product APIs/prototypes/source/clock/pixel-cap changes. Public diagnostic counters have up to 100ms update lag and are submissions, not screen FPS. CDP profile mode is separate and adds overhead. OS/driver caches are not cleared; cold means a fresh app/context, not physical cold GPU.
